sections.description: The service's configuration, bound from the `Orkeon:Host` section. **No secret is ever written here.** A bot token or an API key is referenced by the *name* of an environment variable, never by value — the same rule the LLM providers already follow, and one a chat bot does not get to break.

The Discord channel's configuration. **The token is named, never written.** `DiscordChannelOptions.TokenEnvironmentVariable` holds the *name* of an environment variable; the value never touches the configuration file, a commit or a container image layer. The LLM providers already follow this rule, and a bot token — which can read every message a server sends — does not get an exception.

settings.description: The hosted crews other agents may run, by name — one skill each. None by default.
Serves the exposed crews over A2A. Off, the host listens on no port.
The listener's scheme and host name: `http://localhost` by default, `http://+` for every interface. No port (that is `Port`) and no path.
The listener's port.
Serves the API. Off, the host listens on no port for it.
The most idempotency keys held in memory; the oldest finished ones go first.
How long an idempotency key is remembered. After it, the same key starts a new run.
The most event streams (`GET /runs/{id}/events`) served at once. Beyond it a stream is refused with a 503 `too_many_streams` and a `Retry-After`: each stream holds a connection and polls the history.
The `HttpListener` prefix: scheme, host, port and a closing slash. A host the loopback does not contain (`http://+:5190/`) requires an authentication scheme or mutual TLS under `Security`.

How long a `/readyz` answer is reused before the checks run again. Readiness reaches the state store and the history: a probe loop or a hostile client must not turn each request into that work. Zero runs the checks every time.

Health-check tags added to readiness besides `ready`. `llm` adds the LLM provider check, which reaches an external service: left out by default, so a provider outage does not take the daemon out of rotation.
Authentication schemes accepted: `Bearer` and/or `ApiKey`. Empty means no authentication is required. Each declared scheme is validated, not merely matched (see `A2ACredentialValidator`).
Names of the secrets holding the API keys the `ApiKey` scheme accepts, read through the `ISecretProvider` on every request.
Whether a client certificate chaining to a trust anchor is required (fail-closed without one).
Paths of the CA certificates a client certificate must chain to when mutual TLS is required.
Thumbprints of client certificates pinned exactly (still refused outside their validity window).

How long a quiet event stream waits before it writes a keep-alive frame (an SSE comment, a blank NDJSON line). The write is what detects a client that went away: an abandoned stream of a long run would otherwise live as long as the run.

What the crew does, in a sentence: the description of its skill on the A2A agent card when `Orkeon:Host:A2A` exposes it. Read from the configuration, never from the crew definition — the card is built without loading a crew. Optional.

The folders this host grants THIS crew, as mount strings (`<physical>:<virtual>:<rights>`): a mount namespace of its own for each run, so two hosted crews may both address `/output` over two different folders. Empty (the default) keeps the host's mounts for that crew. A granted folder is an input of the daemon: readable wherever it lies, without `--allow-external-mounts`.
The name the channels and the operator use to refer to it.
Path to the crew definition — a YAML file, a multi-file crew directory, or an `.ork.ts` script. The same targets `orkeon run` accepts.
How many runs of this crew may be in flight at once. Bounded on purpose: a daemon that accepts unlimited concurrent runs is a daemon that dies under its first burst.

The LLM profiles (`Llm:Profiles:<name>`) the hosted crews may name. The service runs crews it does not control: unset, every profile the configuration defines is offered; set, only those listed — a crew naming another one fails to load, the run with it. The default profile (the `Llm` section) is always offered, so `["default"]` offers it alone. Every entry must name a defined profile.

How long a run may take before the host cancels it. A daemon has no user watching to press Ctrl-C, so an unbounded run is a stuck daemon. The clock stops while the run holds on a question to a person: the hold timeout, not this one, ends that wait.
How long the host waits for in-flight runs on shutdown before giving up. Systemd sends SIGKILL after its own timeout, so this must stay under it.
Discord user ids allowed to talk to the bot. **Empty denies everyone** — a bot on a public server with an open door spends someone's API budget on strangers.
The crew a room without a route reaches. Unset, it is the first crew declared under `Orkeon:Host:Crews`; set, it must name one of them.
Whether the channel is switched on. Off unless a deployment says otherwise.

Guild (server) ids to register the slash commands in. **Empty registers them globally**, which needs no configuration but is cached by Discord for up to an hour; naming guilds makes `/status` and `/stop` available immediately — the dev loop.
How long progress updates are spaced out. Discord's rate limit is per channel and unforgiving; a message per agent thought would exhaust it inside one crew.

Which crew each room reaches: a Discord channel id (the channel threads are opened in) mapped to a hosted crew's name. A thread opened in a routed channel starts that crew; a thread anywhere else starts `DefaultCrew`. A route to a crew the host does not declare, or a key that is not a channel id, refuses the start.
Name of the environment variable holding the bot token.
